column1: # HARDEN-REPORT.tsv -- the ledger in the kiosk stack shape (leg layer component source status note); drawn 20261019-204855 from ledger b1e7cf51b3156778

column6: A joining client loads the host's snapshot as raw memory: g_mp.leader, resident and sprite_owner index g_mp.p[4] with no bound, so a hostile host writes 512 chosen bytes about 100 KB past the array (writers: pmo:323;epmo:B7)
SnapData bound check wrapped (off near 2^32 plus n passed, memcpy 4 GB past the buffer) and SnapInfo size 0 divided by zero; both reproduced under ASan (writers: commit:HEAD)

One unauthenticated 34-byte Hello from a spoofed source makes the host stream about 0.5 MB (snapshot plus a Frames packet per tick for 6 s) to that address; three such Hellos per 6 s also hold the game full (writers: pmo:324)

Nothing after Hello is authenticated: packets match a client by ip:port; the 32-bit reconnect token travels in clear; a parked seat is taken by any sender with the same name (reproduced: ./h1 steal) (writers: pmo:324)
ApplyBps trusted the patch past its CRCs: outputOffset was never bounded against dst_size (ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE at util.c:259 with a CRC-valid lying patch) (writers: commit:HEAD)
A joined client can make the host rebuild and resend a snapshot per packet (rejoin=1 Hello, resync Input), pinning CPU and uplink; no rate limit on any packet type (writers: pmo:325)

UPnP/SSDP takes LOCATION, control URL and external IP from whichever device answers first, on any host; a rejected lease retries as permanent (lease 0); STUN replies are taken from any source (writers: pmo:326)

A host-planted save (Keep a copy writes the host's RAM with a good checksum) with a max-health byte under 8 made the file-select draw loop never end, writing past vram_upload_data (writers: commit:HEAD)

Snapshot, save and replay parsers rely on assert (loadFunc bound, StateRecorder version); the vcxproj Release build defines NDEBUG and loses them; RLE output is uncapped (about 270 MB from a 4 MB snapshot) (writers: pmo:327)

A bare host:port on any server but archipelago.gg tries ws:// before wss://, so the slot password and all traffic go in clear with no downgrade needed (reproduced against a plaintext fake server) (writers: pmo:328)
No cap on ReceivedItems, players or slot_info from the server: one 16 MiB message (about 20 KB compressed) cost 700 MB RSS, a second 956 MB (writers: pmo:329)

tcc.exe (a personal fork's release), SDL2.dll and the SDL2 source are fetched over https with no hash and run or shipped: the DLL goes into the Windows artifact players are told to download (writers: pmo:330;epmo:B6)
pip installs are unpinned (pip itself upgraded in one script) and run at the player's privilege, with a system-wide fallback (writers: pmo:330)

saves/ref/*.sav (13 files, 6.5 MB) are full emulator state built from the commercial ROM, inherited from upstream snesrev/zelda3, in a repo whose .gitignore says never to commit Nintendo data (writers: pmo:331)
Every joiner receives the host's whole SRAM, all three save slots and backups, in the join snapshot; the doc said only that joining downloads the host's game (writers: pmo:332)
No SECURITY.md or private report route; blank issues disabled and the bug form invited pasting addresses (writers: commit:HEAD;epmo:B5)
The Windows crash file recorded the faulting module's full path (the player's account folder) and the dialog asked the player to send it (writers: commit:HEAD)

What leaves the machine was not in one place: STUN to Google by default, the room code is the raw address, netplay unencrypted, ws:// first for Archipelago, coop.ini keeps the last friend's address, F12 captures the overlay (writers: commit:HEAD;epmo:B5)

a removed player can't come back on their own was false: kicks matched token or (address, name), so a new name from the same machine was let in (reproduced: ./h1 kick). Now a per-install random id travels in Hello (wire 22) and a host that bans by it (BanByInstallId, default on) keeps the install out and refuses an id-less Hello; either side may switch its half off, and the doc says what each setting buys (writers: commit:HEAD)

The default branch is claude/great-maxwell-00u7q3, so a stranger's clone lands on an AI-session-named branch; README line 13 "room codes instead of IP addresses" reads as hiding the address; BUILDING.md clones upstream and gives SHA256 where the code checks SHA1; AI_DISCLOSURE says every commit has a trailer (two merges and one web deletion do not); CI prints otool -L and asserts nothing (writers: pmo:333)

After a joined game, Reset restores the player's SRAM only when saves/sram.dat opens at 8192 bytes; otherwise the host's SRAM stays in memory and the foreign flag clears, so the next save writes the host's slots to the player's file (read, not run) (writers: pmo:334)

Small items: ReadWholeFile on a FIFO writes one byte before its buffer; ini !include fan-out and shader #include depth unbounded; remote names reach stderr and toasts unfiltered; DSP firBufferIndex unmasked; AP password silently cut at 63 bytes; SSL_set1_host return unchecked; out-of-range double to int casts; build_apworld.py follows symlinks; a test script binds 0.0.0.0; ZELDA3_AP_DEBUG prints the password (writers: pmo:335)
.gitignore missed files the game writes: saves/sram.dat.bak (a save), zelda3_crash.txt, spoiler_*.txt (writers: commit:HEAD)
The workflow had no permissions block, so the token took the repository default; actions and the devkitPro image are pinned by tag only (still open) (writers: commit:HEAD)
get_python_libs.bat was stored with CRLF while .gitattributes says *.bat text eol=crlf, so every fresh clone showed it modified (writers: commit:HEAD)

A per-game random key beside the room code (a secret friends share without a server) would carry H-003, H-004 and the rest of H-019 at once; designed as an optional layer in HARDEN/DESIGN-room-key.md, code not yet written (writers: pmo:324)

The reviewers' harnesses now live in HARDEN/harness (h1.c, bps_h.c, amp.c, fuzzmsg.c, clientdrv.c and the rest) with their build lines; wiring them into CI would let it go red on H-001, H-002, H-005 and H-011 for good (writers: -)
